explanation: The real numbers are the combination of the rational numbers (Q) and the irrational numbers (Q'): R = Q ∪ Q'. A rational number is p/q with integers p, q and q ≠ 0; its decimal terminates (1/4 = 0.25) or repeats (0.333..., 0.939393...). An irrational number like pi = 3.14159..., e = 2.71828... or sqrt(2) = 1.41421... never terminates and never repeats. Together the two families fill the number line completely: every point is exactly one real number, with no gaps.
pakistani_life_example: Shopping for cloth at the bazaar: 2.5 metres of fabric is a terminating decimal (rational), and Rs 480.50 per metre is rational too. But the diagonal of a square courtyard tile of side 1 m is sqrt(2) = 1.41421... metres — it never ends and never repeats (irrational). Both kinds sit together on the same measuring tape: R = Q ∪ Q'.

worked_example.title: Convert the recurring decimal 0.93-bar to p/q form (textbook Example 3)
steps: Check against the textbook: Example 3 lists 0.93-bar = 93/99 = 31/33.
worked_example.citation: PCTB Mathematics-9, page1-150.pdf PDF page 8 (printed page 6), Example 3

practice.prompt: Use the textbook's multiply-and-subtract method: write 0.5-bar (0.555...) in p/q form.
practice.hint: Example 3: let x = 0.555..., multiply by 10 so 10x = 5.555..., then subtract x.
practice.solution: x = 0.555...; 10x = 5.555...; 10x − x = 5, so 9x = 5 and x = 5/9. This matches Example 3's 0.5-bar = 5/9.
practice.citation: Method follows PCTB Mathematics-9, page1-150.pdf PDF page 8 (printed page 6), Example 3

quiz.text: R = Q ∪ Q′. Which numbers belong to Q′?
quiz.explanation: Q' is the set of irrational numbers: decimals that never stop and never repeat, like sqrt(2) = 1.41421..., pi = 3.14159... and e = 2.71828.... Rationals like 0.25 belong to Q, not Q'.
quiz.citation: PCTB Mathematics-9, page1-150.pdf PDF page 3 (printed page 1) for R = Q ∪ Q'; PDF page 6 (printed page 4) for the irrational examples

quiz.explanation: Example 3's method: let x = 0.555..., then 10x = 5.555... Subtracting gives 9x = 5, so x = 5/9 — exactly as the book lists 0.5-bar = 5/9.
quiz.citation: PCTB Mathematics-9, page1-150.pdf PDF page 8 (printed page 6), Example 3

quiz.text: Which pair of rational numbers between 2 and 3 does Example 4 list?
quiz.explanation: Example 4: two rational numbers between 2 and 3 are 5/2 = 2.5 and 11/4 = 2.75. Pi, e, sqrt(2) and sqrt(3) are irrational, so they are not the answer.
quiz.citation: PCTB Mathematics-9, page1-150.pdf PDF page 8 (printed page 6), Example 4

angel_replies.text: Chalo, dobara dekho! R = Q union Q-prime: rationals (decimals that stop or repeat) plus irrationals (decimals that never stop and never repeat). The line is full — no gaps!
Hint: for a recurring decimal, let it equal x, multiply by 10 or 100 to shift the pattern, subtract, then divide. Try it on 0.555... first.
Test ready! Three questions: Q-prime ka matlab, 0.5-bar as a fraction, and Example 4's two rationals between 2 and 3. Bismillah!
Koi baat nahi! Check two things: does the decimal stop or repeat (that makes it rational), and did you shift the pattern by the right power of 10 before subtracting?
Himmat rakho! Example 3 ka method bas teen steps hai: shift, subtract, divide. Ek aur try — main saath hoon.
Main Angel hoon — aapki numbers wali dost! Salam! Ready ho to slides chalao ya 'test lo' keh do.

slides.narration: Dekho, R = Q union Q-prime! Q holds the rationals — p/q numbers whose decimals stop or repeat. Q-prime holds the irrationals — pi, e, sqrt(2), never ending, never repeating. Union karo, and the number line is completely full: every point is exactly one real number. (PCTB Mathematics-9, PDF page 3, printed page 1)

checkpoints.question: R is the union of Q and Q′. What lives in Q′?
checkpoints.hint: Q holds the p/q numbers. Q′ is the other family on the line.
checkpoints.correct_feedback: Irrational numbers — like pi, e, sqrt(2) (PDF page 3).
checkpoints.retry_feedback: Q′ is what is NOT rational: the never-ending, never-repeating numbers.

slides.narration: Repeating decimals are rational! Example 3: x = 0.555..., multiply by 10: 10x = 5.555..., subtract: 9x = 5, so x = 5/9. Same trick with two repeating digits: 0.939393... = 0.93-bar = 93/99 = 31/33. Shift, subtract, divide! (PCTB Mathematics-9, PDF page 8, printed page 6)
slides.caption: Repeating decimals are rational

checkpoints.question: 0.555... = 0.5-bar. What is it as p/q?

slides.narration: Rationals are dense — between any two you find more! Example 4: two rational numbers between 2 and 3 are 5/2 = 2.5 and 11/4 = 2.75. Halves aur quarters — infinitely many exist. (PCTB Mathematics-9, PDF page 8, printed page 6)
